insights.title:
What we are
working on
insights.text: Not a blog, a work log. Whatever is on our desk this week is written here.

aePanel.title: A separate panel for companies
aePanel.excerpt: We are building the employer's own workspace at panel.anlikeleman.com. Posting shifts, reviewing applications, messaging candidates and tracking workers all sit in one panel.

body.p1: On Anlık Eleman the employer side is a product of its own, just like the worker side. So we are building a separate panel for companies at panel.anlikeleman.com.
body.p2: In the panel an employer posts a shift, sees every application in one list, messages candidates and tracks workers day by day. The goal is to cut the steps needed to fill a shift.
body.p3: The panel runs on the same data as the mobile app. When an application lands, the employer sees it on the phone and in the panel at the same moment.

aeMobile.title: iOS and Android from one codebase
aeMobile.excerpt: We build the mobile app for both stores together. Notifications, location and the application flow behave the same on each platform.

body.p1: We build the mobile app for iOS and Android from a single codebase. Two stores, one team, one release flow.
body.p2: Notifications, location permissions and the application flow behave the same on both platforms. Platform-specific differences stay only where the system demands them.
body.p3: This lets us ship a new feature to both platforms within the same week.

aeWeb.title: Fewer steps on the web
aeWeb.excerpt: We are simplifying the flow for job seekers: pick your free days, see nearby listings, apply from a single screen. Web and mobile move together.

body.p1: On the web we are rebuilding the job seeker flow to be simpler. Pick your free days, see nearby listings, apply from one screen.
body.p2: The old flow spread an application across several steps. By merging steps and shortening the form we expect fewer people to drop out before finishing.
body.p3: Web and mobile move together; both sides use the same screens and the same language.

barbarosServer.title: Server and Unity in the same rhythm
barbarosServer.excerpt: On the MMO side we develop the game server, API and database in sync with the Unity client. Every new mechanic lands on the server first, then becomes playable in the game.

body.p1: In Barbaros: Kızıl Sakal the rules of the game run on the server. Unity carries the visuals, the controls and the feel.
body.p2: We develop the game server, API and database in sync with the Unity client. A new mechanic lands in the data model and on the server first, then becomes playable in the game.
body.p3: That order is what keeps everyone at sea seeing the same truth: whether a shot lands is decided by the server, not the client.

barbarosMaps.title: Building the maps in Unity
barbarosMaps.excerpt: We produce the game world's maps on the Unity side: islands, ports, open sea areas and the crossings between maps.

body.p1: We produce the game world's maps on the Unity side. Islands, ports, open sea areas and the crossings between maps are each built by hand.
body.p2: A map is not only a visual space. Which region is more dangerous, where loot appears and where you cross into another map are all decided at this stage.
body.p3: The aim is a sea that stays readable and fast with hundreds of ships on screen at once.

process.title: Meet, make sense of it, move
process.excerpt: Regular meetings keep what we are building and why it matters fresh on every project. We sharpen the scope, cut the work into small pieces and keep the process visible to everyone involved.

body.p1: Regular meetings keep what we are building and why it matters fresh on every project.
body.p2: We sharpen the scope and cut the work into small pieces, so every step leaves something visible and working.
body.p3: We keep the process open: where we are, what is waiting and what comes next is always clear.

overview.p1: Anlık Eleman brings people looking for daily or seasonal work together with the businesses that need them. Workers pick the days they are free, see nearby listings and apply in a single flow. Employers post a shift, review applications and message candidates directly.
overview.p2: Right now the weight is on interface and experience. We are cutting steps out of the application flow, building a mobile dashboard for employers and moving web and mobile forward together, so both sides speak the same language.

overview.p1: Nappsa is a suggestion app built to lighten the small decisions of the day. What to eat, what to watch, what to do: it answers each with a short, curated set of ideas.
overview.p2: The goal is not an endless list but an easier choice. Suggestions refresh daily and take you to one decision instead of a long search.

overview.p1: Tilo is a calm puzzle game that turns your own photos into jigsaws. Pick a shot, break it into pieces and finish it at your own pace.
overview.p2: No timers, no streaks, no pressure. It is built for a rhythm you can open during a short break, place a few pieces and pick up again later.

overview.p1: Grid Grin is a classic block puzzle where you drop blocks onto the board and clear rows and columns. The rules read in seconds, mastery takes longer.
overview.p2: Instead of time pressure it runs on making space and setting up combos. Your real opponent is your own high score.

overview.p1: Barbaros: Kızıl Sakal is a top-down, real-time multiplayer sea world drawing on the seafaring era between 1300 and 1500. You start with a small boat and work your way to larger ships and deeper waters through quests, battles and trade.
overview.p2: It is not a single battle arena. Exploration, naval combat, equipment progression, trade and fleet politics all share one sea. It is designed as a long-running MMO: the point is not to win a match but to make a name for yourself out there.

factions.title: Two sides, two worlds
factions.description: Pirates and Cities stand against each other. Each has its own starting region, ships, architecture and characters. The side you pick decides how the sea greets you.

classes.title: One ship, four captains
classes.description: Gonzales plays on speed and manoeuvring, Marta on healing and support, Zoro on raw damage, Bruno on holding the front line. Because the ship's look is independent of the class, the same vessel can produce two completely different play styles.

combat.title: The right shot at the right moment
combat.description: Cannons and harpoons sit at the centre of combat, but ammunition makes the difference. Some rounds slow, some break armour, some leave fire or poison, some cut off the enemy's healing. The winner is not the biggest gun but the right choice in the moment.

ships.title: From small boat to flagship
ships.description: Across ten ship tiers the hull grows, the cannon count rises and sails and ornaments change. Sails, rudder, hull, figurehead and crew all upgrade separately. Upgrading carries risk: the higher the level the lower the odds, which is what makes a good part genuinely valuable.

world.title: The sea behind the fog
world.description: The map is not open from the start. Everything outside your line of sight is covered by fog of war, so spotting a rival first is an advantage. The server opens up more dangerous, more rewarding regions from time to time. Chests, sea monsters, bosses and fishing are scattered across this world.

social.title: From party to fleet
social.description: Parties of up to six ships turn into lasting fleets over time. Fleets can hold islands, raise defence towers and fight for control of a region. A player-run market keeps that balance moving.

tech.text: The rules of the game run on the server, while Unity carries the visuals, the controls and the feel. Whether a shot lands is decided by the server, not the client, so everyone at sea sees the same truth. Lasting progress and live battle data sit in separate layers, so the system can grow as the world does.

status.text: The project is past the concept stage. The backbone of movement, combat, skills, NPCs, loot, equipment, parties and fleets is in place. The weight now is on connecting those systems, measuring performance, producing content and raising visual and audio quality.

aboutPage.title:
We turn ideas into
digital products that work
aboutPage.lead: Tecktick Labs is a technology studio based in Istanbul. We build mobile apps, web platforms, backend systems and custom software.
aboutPage.journeyTitle:
A new company,
not a new track record
aboutPage.journeyText: The company is at the start of its journey. Behind it sits development history that runs from enterprise projects to mobile apps, from business platforms to real-time systems.
aboutPage.approachTitle: How we look at a project
aboutPage.approachText: We do not treat a project as something to write code for. First we understand the need and the people using it, then we cut needless complexity and ship something sustainable. Design, software, data, integrations and release are handled as one whole.

clarity.title: Being understood
clarity.description: We explain what we are doing and why in plain language. When detail is needed we are the people you talk to, not a layer in between.

ownership.title: Taking ownership
ownership.description: The work does not end at handover. We watch how it behaves in the wild, what breaks and how it gets used.

craft.title: Craft
craft.description: Speed matters, rushing does not. A build that runs smoothly, opens fast and reads clearly is part of the result.

aboutPage.ownText: Alongside client work we build our own products. That keeps us judging a product not only on its engineering, but on user experience, operations, growth and whether it holds up over time.
aboutPage.workText: We understand the problem, build the right system, ship something that works and keep improving it with real feedback.
